DRAMADIRECTOR.title: Drama Director

intro.title: Title
intro.subtitle: Subtitle
intro.sincityDesc: Noir-style intro. Campaign name at an angle, characters in strict B/W silhouettes, names in red with white outline. Finale — 'Directed by' with GM name.
intro.snatchDesc: Guy Ritchie style intro. Campaign name, then each character: portrait with instant duotone transition on random colored background. Finale — 'Directed by'.
intro.macheteDesc: 70s Grindhouse cinema intro. Reverse film countdown, warm amber palette, lobby cards with film scratches and cigarette burns.
intro.scifiDesc: Classic sci-fi cinematic intro. HUD interface animations over a space backdrop, character introductions one by one with retro science-fiction film typography. Finale — 'Mission Commence' with GM callsign.
intro.detectiveDesc: Noir detective cinematic intro. A dark screen with a flashlight beam that sweeps from the corner to the center, illuminating the campaign title in the Scare font. The flashlight flickers occasionally.
intro.detectiveLine1: Detective: I don't know why you need them, but this is no simple task..
intro.detectiveLine2: Detective: {name}, so why did you need them?
intro.macheteBloodDesc: Screen slowly fills with blood from top to bottom. Accompanied by evil laughter.
intro.hint: Choose a cinematic intro style below. The Campaign Name field is used for some intro animations. Select a target player or leave blank to show to all.

endings.wbrbDesc: Freeze frame + Eric Andre style title card. Screen desaturates and freezes, the text appears instantly in the top-left corner.
endings.jojoDesc: Classic anime-style ending: freeze frame, character portraits, credits with player names and GM production credit.
endings.hint: Play a cinematic end-of-session card for all players. WBRB pauses the scene, JoJo shows a dramatic freeze-frame ending.

video.hint: Video is shown on top of the screen for all players (or selected one). GM sees the ✕ button to close.
video.instructionHint: Select a video file (mp4/webm) using the folder button or paste a path directly. Set loop and volume, then press Play. Use Stop to close the player on all screens.

vn.desc: Full-screen VN overlay on top of the scene.
vn.features:
• Up to 20 characters (10 left, 10 right)
• Auto-activation by microphone — highlights the speaker
• Speech recognition → subtitles for all players
• Background presets, rosters and full scenes
vn.launchLocalTitle: Open VN only for yourself (no broadcast to players)
vn.charEmpty: No characters added. Click '+ Left' or '+ Right'.
vn.dlgGmHint: When GM speaks — selected character activates. Subtitles go in their name.
vn.micHint: Microphone turns on automatically when VN launches. Each player grants access in their browser.
vn.micSpeechHint: Text is recognized and shown as subtitles in the dialogue window for all players.
vn.helpLaunchText1: Click the Launch VN button in the panel header. The overlay appears for all players simultaneously. Close with the Close VN button or the red button on the overlay.
vn.helpLaunchText2: The For Self button opens VN only for you (GM), without broadcasting to players. Useful for preparing a scene before showing.
vn.helpBgItem1: Paste the file path manually or click to select via file browser. Supports images (jpg, png, webp) and videos (mp4, webm).
vn.helpBgItem2: Fit — how background fits the screen: cover crops edges, contain shows fully with bars, fill stretches.
vn.helpBgItem3: Background Color — underlay color, visible if image is smaller than screen.
vn.helpBgItem4: Dim — semi-transparent black layer over background (0 = none, 1 = fully black).
vn.helpBgItem5: Quick Select — click a tile to instantly apply background. Active tile is highlighted gold. Use search field to filter.
vn.helpBgItem6: Add button lets you create custom background groups with multiple variants (day/night, etc.).
vn.helpCharsItem1: + Left and + Right buttons add a character to the corresponding side of the screen.
vn.helpCharsItem2: Player field — link character to a Foundry user. When that player speaks into the mic — character activates automatically.
vn.helpCharsItem3: Visibility (Visible checkbox) — hidden characters don't appear on overlay but remain in the list.
vn.helpCharsItem5: Scale, X, Y — positioning and size of character on stage.
vn.helpCharsItem6: button — activate character (highlighted, others dimmed). Active character is slightly enlarged.
vn.helpCharsItem7: button — move character from left side to right and back.
vn.helpCharsItem8: buttons — change order in row.
vn.helpCharsItem9: Rosters (at bottom of tab) — save current character set under a name, load later with one click.
vn.helpDlgItem1: Fill in Speaker and text, then click Show — dialogue window appears for all players.
vn.helpDlgItem2: From active button — automatically inserts name and color of currently active character.
vn.helpDlgItem3: Auto-close — dialogue hides after specified seconds (0 = manual).
vn.helpMicItem1: Microphone turns on automatically when VN launches. Each user must grant browser access.
vn.helpMicItem2: Volume Threshold — minimum sound level to detect speech. Increase if character activates from background noise, decrease if not responding to quiet voice.
vn.helpMicItem3: When a player speaks — their character (linked via Player field) is automatically highlighted on stage for everyone.
vn.helpMicItem4: Recognized speech is displayed as subtitles inside the dialogue window.
vn.helpMicItem5: button in top right corner of overlay lets you quickly toggle microphone during play.
vn.helpGmBarText: Appears on the left side of screen only for GM when VN is active.
vn.helpGmBarItem1: Speaking — select which character GM speaks as. When GM speaks into mic — this character highlights and subtitles go in their name.
vn.helpGmBarItem2: Actors button — opens/closes list of all scene characters:
vn.helpGmBarItem2a: LMB on character — show / hide them on stage
vn.helpGmBarItem2b: RMB on character — move from left side to right and back
vn.helpGmBarItem2c: button — activate / deactivate character
vn.helpGmBarItem2d: Player dropdown — link character to user directly from left panel
vn.helpGmBarItem3: Backgrounds button — opens quick list of all backgrounds. Click a background — it applies immediately. Active background has gold stripe on left.
vn.helpGmBarItem4: Both sections have search in real time.
vn.helpQuickBarItem1: Buttons in top right corner of overlay are available to all users.
vn.helpQuickBarItem3: — open Chat in separate window
vn.helpQuickBarItem4: — open Actors in separate window
vn.helpQuickBarItem5: — open Scenes in separate window
vn.helpQuickBarItem6: — open Playlists in separate window
vn.helpQuickBarItem7: — open Items in separate window
vn.helpPresetsItem1: Scene presets — save complete VN state: background, all characters with settings, dialogue parameters. Convenient for prepared scenes.
vn.helpPresetsItem2: Character rosters (on Characters tab) — save only character composition without background.
vn.helpLayersText: Layers allow you to add text and images on top of the VN scene. They are positioned independently of characters.
vn.helpLayersItem1: + Image — add an image layer. Specify the path to the file or use the file browser.
vn.helpLayersItem2: + Text — add a text layer. Enter the text in the field that appears.
vn.helpLayersItem3: X, Y — position of the layer on the screen (in pixels, 1920×1080 canvas).
vn.helpLayersItem4: Z — z-index: the higher the value, the higher the layer is above others.
vn.helpLayersItem5: W, H — width and height of the layer (for images).
vn.helpLayersItem8: Visible — checkbox to show/hide the layer without deleting it.
vn.helpLayersItem9: Buttons — change the order of layers in the list.
vn.helpLayersItem10: Presets — save and load sets of layers for reuse.
vn.helpInteractiveText: Interactive images are clickable and hover-responsive objects placed on the VN scene. They can trigger macros on click or show an alternate image on hover.
vn.helpInteractiveItem1: Add an object — go to the Interactive tab and click «+».
vn.helpInteractiveItem2: Main image — always visible. Hover image — shown when the cursor is over the object (requires On Hover).
vn.helpInteractiveItem3: On Hover — swaps the image on hover. On Click — toggles the image on click.
vn.helpInteractiveItem4: Macro — pick any world macro; it fires when players click the image.
vn.helpInteractiveItem5: Position & size — use X/Y/Z/W/H sliders or drag directly on the scene.
vn.helpInteractiveItem6: Presets — save/restore only position and visibility; objects are never removed when loading a preset.
vn.helpApiText: You can control VN from Foundry macros:

macro.noCharsYet: Add characters in the Characters tab to see them here

gml.playerControlHint: Players can drag their linked portraits
gml.infiniteRosterHint: Remove side limits. All characters spawn at center.

vn.helpMouseScroll: Cycle through overlapping objects under the cursor to select one
vn.helpMouseDrag: Move selected object freely on the stage
vn.helpEmotionsText: The emotion system lets you define a set of portrait images per character and switch between them quickly during play.
vn.helpEmotionsItem1: Add an emotion — open a character in the Characters tab, click «+» next to the Emotions section, enter a name and select an image.
vn.helpEmotionsItem2: Apply an emotion (GM) — click the button next to a character in the GM left bar to open the emotion list with previews.
vn.helpEmotionsItem3: Apply an emotion (player) — click the button in the overlay. Opens a menu with the full list and a favourites section.
vn.helpEmotionsItem4: Favourite wheel — press the middle mouse button. Opens a quick ring menu of star-marked emotions. Star an emotion by clicking ★ next to it.
vn.helpEmotionsItem5: Reset emotion — choose «Reset» in the list or click the centre of the wheel. The character reverts to the base portrait.
vn.helpEmotionsItem6: Macros — use DDVNApi.setEmotion(charId, 'name') to change emotions via Foundry scripts. Character IDs are shown in the Macros tab.
vn.helpAutoSaveText: The VN automatically saves the full scene state when closed and restores it on next open.
vn.helpAutoSaveItem1: Auto Save fires when you click «Close VN» — saves a full snapshot: characters, background, layers, and dialogue.
vn.helpAutoSaveItem2: Auto Load happens when you open VN. The most recent save is loaded: if the last action was a QuickSave (), that is loaded; otherwise the Auto Save is used.
vn.helpAutoSaveItem3: The badge next to the Quick Save button flashes on auto-save and stays visible after load.
vn.helpDepthText: Depth Mode creates a perspective illusion: characters placed lower on the stage appear larger (closer), those higher appear smaller (further away). Enable it from the GM left panel when Mouse Control is active.
vn.helpDepthItem1: Scale Speed — controls how dramatically size changes with vertical position. At 1× scale changes smoothly; higher values make the effect more pronounced.
vn.helpDepthItem2: Y Speed — multiplier for vertical mouse movement. Increase to make dragging characters up/down more sensitive.
vn.helpDepthItem3: Base Scale (on each character/layer) — the reference size at the horizon. The actual rendered scale = Base Scale × perspective factor at that Y position.
vn.helpDepthItem4: The icon next to Scale in Characters and Layers tabs indicates that the slider controls Base Scale in depth mode, not final scale.
vn.helpDepthItem5: To disable depth mode uncheck the Depth Mode checkbox. Characters return to their Base Scale values.
vn.helpHorizonItem1: When Horizon Line is enabled, a fixed vanishing point is set at a specific vertical percentage of the stage (default 30% from top).
vn.helpHorizonItem2: Characters at or above the horizon appear at near-zero scale. Characters at the very bottom of the stage appear at maximum scale.
vn.helpHorizonItem3: Horizon Y % slider (0–90%) moves the horizon up or down. 0% = top edge, 50% = middle of stage.
vn.helpHorizonItem4: The horizon line also constrains vertical movement: characters cannot be dragged above their starting position if they are already at or near the horizon.
vn.charsHint: Add characters to the left, center, or right side. Each character can have a default image and an active image (shown when speaking). Link to a player so their voice activates the character automatically via microphone.
vn.layersHint: Layers sit on top of the scene independently of characters. X/Y in pixels on a 1920×1080 canvas. Z controls stacking order. Lock a layer to prevent accidental changes.
vn.dialogueHint: Type the speaker name and dialogue text, then click Show. The dialogue box appears for all players. Use «From active» to auto-fill the currently highlighted character's name and color.
vn.charInspectorHint: Click a character to edit their settings
vn.presetsSceneHint: Save and load complete scene snapshots — characters, backgrounds, layers and interactive images.
vn.depthModeTitle: Depth mode — objects scale with vertical position

steps.hint: GM detects token movement and broadcasts spatial step sounds to all players
steps.realisticDesc: Random pitch & volume variation each step
steps.fadeDurationHint: Sound fades linearly from full volume to silence over this window (ms). Does not affect step frequency.
steps.spatialDesc: Full directional sound: left, right, front, behind, diagonals — works best with headphones
steps.wallsDesc: How walls between token and listener affect volume
steps.wallHintNone: Walls have no effect on footstep volume.
steps.wallHintBlock: Any wall between source and listener completely silences the sound.
steps.wallHintAttenuate: Each wall on the path halves the volume. Three or more walls = complete silence.
steps.regionsHint: Assign a footstep sound to specific scene regions. When a token enters a region its sound overrides the default; when it exits it reverts.
steps.regionsEmpty: No regions configured. Add a binding below.
steps.regionExists: A region with that name is already configured.
steps.regionDistHint: Distances are optional — leave blank to use the global settings.
steps.soundRegionsHint: Assign a footstep surface to a specific scene region. The surface plays while the token is inside; default resumes on exit.
steps.distRegionsHint: Override the fade distances for footsteps inside a specific region. Sound regions and distance regions are independent and can overlap freely.
steps.distRegionsFieldHint: At least one field is required. Leave blank to inherit the global setting.

recorder.inactiveHint: Enable auto-recording to activate the session finale
recorder.noClipsYet: No clips recorded yet! Enable auto-recording and play a session.
